title: BootstrapRequest
description: What the control plane hands Repo Factory when a PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP run reaches Phase A (PRD §13.1). It carries intent; it does not carry runtime state, because Repo Factory owns no session, provider or scheduling fact.

seed.description: The natural-language project seed, as the owner or Hermes stated it.

repositories.description: Repository intents. One bootstrap operation may cover more than one repository (PRD §16.4), and each carries its own receipts and partial state.

visibility.description: Intent only. Public exposure is an owner gate regardless of what this says (PRD §7 Phase F).

remoteOwner.description: The GitHub account the repositories are created under. Absent means the deployment default. It lives in the request rather than in deployment configuration because the Plan digest has to determine the effect: two identical requests must not compile to the same Plan and then create repositories under different accounts.

humanGateFacts.description: What is already known to require an owner decision, so Phase F does not rediscover it.

channel.description: Which ingress admitted the request. Channel name only — never the actor value, which is an identity the receipt already binds.

name.description: Repository name only. A remote is resolved during planning; a name that already exists with different provenance is a RESOURCE_COLLISION rather than a resume (PRD §16.3).

stack.description: Absent means the plan must resolve it. An unknown stack requires a reviewed custom template and is never silently defaulted to Node (PRD §14.1).
